prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
UK Independence Party Manifesto 2005 – Summary (ideological framing preserved)

- Core purpose: Take back democratic self-government from Brussels by withdrawing from the EU; only then can Britain set its own laws, control borders, cut red tape, and revive prosperity. Not anti-European—pro British self-rule.

- Why leave: The EU is a political project centralising control over laws, policing, justice, defence, and foreign policy; it is undemocratic, corrupt, unreformable, and smothers enterprise with intrusive regulation. Old parties won’t change this one-way drift.

- Independence plan: Repeal the European Communities Act, end UK payments to the EU, restore supremacy of UK law, rejoin global bodies independently (e.g., WTO), and run a two-year transition to replace EU-derived rules and policies (CAP, CFP).

- Trade: Keep free trade with Europe via bilateral deals (as non-EU countries do) and deepen links with NAFTA nations, the Commonwealth, and fast-growing regions. Mutual cooperation on environment/residency continues without EU membership.

- Deregulation: Scrap or pare back most EU-origin rules—especially those crippling SMEs—unless there’s an overwhelming case to keep them. End gold-plating and burdens like the Working Time Directive.

- Budget and tax: Redirect the UK’s EU contribution to raise the state pension by £2/week. Temporarily borrow £3bn/year to fund immediate tax cuts and targeted spending. Immediate tax steps: halve council tax for all; scrap the 10% income tax band; reinstate the dividend tax credit; raise IHT threshold to £500k. Long-term: simplify radically—merge NI with income tax, replace VAT with a wholesale sales tax, consider a low flat tax to spur growth.

- NHS: End central micromanagement and target-chasing; restore local control and the matron system; empower clinicians to treat by need; reopen GP surgeries out of hours; cut bureaucracy. Allow complementary private insurance; lift EU curbs on supplements and hours.

- Welfare and pensions: Simplify benefits, reduce means-testing, and restore independence from welfare dependency. Reinstate pension fund dividend credits (+£5bn/year), raise state pensions £2/week, unfreeze expat pensions; long term, save more/work longer—not mass immigration.

- Schools and universities: Give schools autonomy; scrap SATs and the QCA; back discipline, selection, specialisation, sports, and trips. Expand assisted places, vouchers/tax relief for parental choice. Universities: close weak courses, fully fund strong ones; cancel top-up fees, restore grants, scrap loans; charge EU students full fees; boost technical colleges.

- Law and order: Local accountability of police; less paperwork; credible sentencing; stronger magistrates; more prisons; protect homeowners. Reject EU Corpus Juris and a European prosecutor.

- Immigration: Target near-zero net migration. One points-based system for all countries (EU and non-EU alike); tighter family routes; embarkation controls; “Britishness” tests; health checks; safe-third-country rule; enforce removals; adjust human-rights law as needed. No quotas.

- Farming and fishing: Leave CAP; bring back deficiency payments/price guarantees; curb big-buyer power; consider reviving the Milk Marketing Board; reward green/hill farming; enable diversification; promote local food. Quit CFP; reclaim and enforce UK waters; ban destructive practices; use fallow zones.

- Defence/foreign: Deploy only in the national interest; reverse cuts; buy British where possible; stay in NATO; leave EU defence plans; keep an independent UN seat.

- Energy/environment/transport: Stop windfarm roll-out; build new nuclear; pursue clean coal and fusion. Repatriate environmental policy; back recycling and protect countryside; ban GM crop planting until proven safe. Fund roads; free transport from EU diktats; improve rail with structures that work; raise speed limits where safe; use speed cameras only for genuine safety.

- Governance and society: Uphold Commons, Lords, monarchy, and common law; resist further dilution of the Lords. Binding referendums when 5% of voters petition. English votes for English laws. Scrap regional assemblies/quangos; return business rates/stamp duty to councils; focus on core local services. Repeal the Human Rights Act; reject EU Charter; drop ID cards; repeal the Hunting Act. Revive trust, responsibility, family, and pride through independence, deregulation, and free trade.
